title: Replacing a Main Shutoff Valve: Curb Stop to Ball Valve and Soldered Joint

locations.name: Indoor fixture shutoffs (under sinks and toilets)
locations.basis: Transcript notes that service valves exist on fixtures and inside the house.

locations.name: Curb stop/shutoff at street-front (outdoor main supply)
locations.basis: Transcript describes an external main shutoff located down below the frost line and accessible via curb cap and a specialized wrench.

summary: This instructional video demonstrates replacing a malfunctioning main shutoff valve by first acknowledging an exterior curb stop at the street-front, coordinating with the local water department to shut/reopen service, and then installing a modern ball valve. The presenter explains the external curb-cap access, introduces the ball valve with its directional flow, and shows copper-pipe prep with flux, a tight-space cutting tool, and a soldering technique to create a watertight joint. After installation, the water is restored and tested to verify proper operation.
topics: Curb cap and curb box access
Copper pipe cutting (imp cutter for tight spaces)
Copper pipe cleaning and flux application
System drainage and purging before soldering

sections.title: Identify curb stop and exterior shutoff location
sections.description: Introduces the idea that a main external shutoff exists at the street-front, often buried below frost depth, with a curb cap and a specialized tool to access it. Also notes existing indoor shutoffs and fixture valves.

sections.title: Plan and begin replacement with a ball valve
sections.description: The plan shifts to replacing the old shutoff with a modern ball valve. The presenter explains how a ball valve operates (closed = no flow; open = full-port) and describes cutting in the new valve to create space for a soldered connection.

sections.title: Soldering, testing, and reactivation
sections.description: Covers preparatory steps (pipe cleaning, flux application), using a tight-space cutter, performing a side solder, then reactivating water service and testing to confirm a watertight joint and proper valve operation.

featured_techniques.technique: Access curb stop via curb cap and curb box with a specialized wrench
Install a modern ball valve on the main supply and explain its operation (directional flow, full-port when open)
Prepare copper pipe for a soldered joint: clean, flux, heat, and apply solder for a watertight seal
Drain and purge the system to allow safe soldering of the new joint (venting and water removal from the line)
Post-installation test: restore water, open fixtures, and verify lack of leaks
